questions.q: What does the Beginner project's existing Gold table, gold.daily_sales_summary, hold?
options: One row per store per day, with total_sales and total_transactions
One row per store, category, and day, with total_sales and total_quantity
One row per category across the entire company, with no store breakdown
One row per transaction, with every raw column from the source file
questions.explain: gold.daily_sales_summary was built at the store/day grain for Store Operations — no category dimension at all.

questions.q: What does the Regional Manager's new request actually require?
options: Nothing new — the existing Gold table already answers this question
Deleting gold.daily_sales_summary because it was built wrong
A new Gold table broken out by category, since the existing table has no category dimension
Switching the whole pipeline from Delta Lake to a different storage format
questions.explain: gold.daily_sales_summary can't answer a category-breakdown question because it was deliberately built without a category dimension. The fix is a new Gold table, not a fix to a broken one.

questions.q: What kind of problem is the nightly full reload running too long, according to this lesson?
options: A scale problem — the design is still correct, it just gets slower as the data grows
A correctness problem — the numbers coming out of the pipeline are wrong
A hardware failure in the Spark cluster
A security problem — unauthorized users are querying Bronze
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: this is not a correctness problem. The output is still right; the design just no longer scales within the overnight batch window.

questions.q: Why does this lesson insist on treating the two problems separately before planning a fix?
options: Because only one of the two problems is actually real
Because Delta Lake requires every table to be fixed one at a time
Because the Regional Manager's request caused the nightly job to slow down
Because they have genuinely different causes, even though they end up sharing one solution
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly separates 'new requirement' from 'doesn't scale' as two different problems with different causes, even though the incremental redesign ends up solving both.

questions.q: Why does the nightly job's runtime keep growing, specifically?
options: Because the Regional Manager added more stores to the chain
Because it reprocesses the full accumulated history in bronze.sales_raw every night, not just the new data
Because the source files are stored in the wrong file format
Because gold.category_breakdown is too large to query quickly
questions.explain: The nightly pipeline reprocesses all of bronze.sales_raw's accumulated history every run, so runtime grows with total history, not with what's actually new.
